milestones.brief:
Implement the placeholder scanner in tool.py for a small build-notice renderer. The CLI, input validation and expansion skeleton are provided; parse_pattern currently treats everything as plain text. Python standard library only; no installs, network or persistent files.

Input has exactly {"action":"render","pattern":STRING,"bindings":{KEY:STRING,...}}. Keys match ASCII [a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,23}. Pattern is at most 1024 characters; bindings has at most 32 keys and each value at most 256 characters. Pattern and binding values must be ASCII strings; tabs/newlines encoded in JSON are allowed. Empty strings/maps and unused bindings are valid. Wrong fields, types, ranges or non-ASCII text yield {"fault":"request"}.

${key} substitutes its binding. Scan left to right: each $$ pair emits one literal dollar and cannot open a placeholder. All other characters, including a dollar not followed by $ or {, remain literal. An opener ${ must have a closing } and contain exactly a valid key; otherwise return {"fault":"pattern"}. Validate the entire pattern before resolving fields; a malformed later placeholder beats an earlier missing binding. In this first release, a missing binding yields {"fault":"missing","key":KEY} for the first unresolved occurrence. Substituted values are literal text: do not parse them again or strip whitespace.

Success is {"text":STRING}. After all substitutions, more than 1536 output characters yields {"fault":"size"}. No partial text accompanies a fault. Emit one JSON result and exit zero for all specified application errors.

Public smoke:
Input: {"action":"render","pattern":"Edited ${unit}: $$${verb}.","bindings":{"unit":"scanner","verb":"ready"}}
Output: {"text":"Edited scanner: $ready."}

Extend tool.py's build-notice renderer with filters and a missing-binding policy option. Preserve the existing scanner, validation, size limit and one-JSON-result CLI. Python standard library only.

A placeholder may have exactly one filter, upper or lower, written as ${key|upper} or ${key|lower}. Filters transform the substituted ASCII value only, preserving nonletters. Plain ${key} still works. Unknown filters, multiple filters, or an empty key/filter yield {"fault":"pattern"}.

Policy correction: the old unconditional missing-binding error is superseded. The default missing-binding policy is now keep: preserve the complete original placeholder, including any filter, literally. The render request may now also include optional "missing", exactly "keep", "error" or "empty". keep is the default; error retains the previous first-missing fault; empty substitutes an empty string for unresolved placeholders. Do not apply filters to preserved placeholders.

Keep the previous dollar escaping, pattern-error precedence and literal-substitution behavior. Extra fields remain invalid; all faults keep their existing shapes. Current brief/source override an obsolete remembered default.

Public smoke:
Input: {"action":"render","pattern":"${label|upper} / ${pending|lower}","bindings":{"label":"draft"}}
Output: {"text":"DRAFT / ${pending|lower}"}

milestones.brief:
Add a template inspection action to the build-notice tool in tool.py; preserve render, including its current options and corrected default. Standard library only; no installs, network or persistent state.

New input: {"action":"inspect","pattern":STRING,"available":[KEY,...]}. Reuse the existing pattern grammar and size/ASCII validation. available is a list of at most 32 distinct valid binding keys; wrong shapes, duplicates or extra fields yield {"fault":"request"}. Invalid pattern syntax still yields {"fault":"pattern"}.

Return {"uses":[{"name":KEY,"count":N,"forms":[FORM,...]},...],"unbound":[KEY,...],"unused":[KEY,...]}. uses has one row per actual placeholder name, in first-occurrence order. Count every occurrence, including repeated filtered uses. forms is the lexicographically sorted set of forms used for that name: "plain" for no filter, otherwise the filter name. unbound lists used names absent from available, in uses order. unused lists available names never used, in the supplied available order. Literal text contributes no uses. Empty collections are valid.

Inspection does not substitute any values and does not accept bindings or missing options. Missing names are diagnostics, not render faults. No normalization or alternate parsing rules are added.

Public smoke:
Input: {"action":"inspect","pattern":"${file} -> ${file|upper} (${kind})","available":["file","spare"]}
Output: {"uses":[{"name":"file","count":2,"forms":["plain","upper"]},{"name":"kind","count":1,"forms":["plain"]}],"unbound":["kind"],"unused":["spare"]}

milestones.brief:
Implement dependency ordering in tool.py for a local asset-bundle manifest checker. Validation and a JSON CLI are provided; resolve() is an unfinished placeholder. Only Python standard library; do not build assets, touch persistent files, install packages or use the network.

Input has exactly {"command":"order","nodes":[{"name":NAME,"requires":[NAME,...]},...]}. At most 32 nodes and 32 prerequisites per node. Names match ASCII [a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,19}; node names are unique. Every prerequisite must name a declared node. Repeated names in one requires list are invalid, not redundant edges to silently deduplicate. Empty manifests/lists are valid; self-dependencies and longer cycles are valid graphs, not schema errors.

Output is {"ordered":[NAME,...],"blocked":[NAME,...]}. A node may be emitted only after all of its declared prerequisites have been emitted; requires points to prerequisites, not consumers. For this initial release, when several nodes are ready, emit the one appearing earliest in the supplied manifest. Reconsider readiness after each emitted node; do not finish an old batch of ready nodes first. When progress stops, blocked contains every unfinished node in manifest order, including acyclic dependents of a cycle; keep independently completed nodes in ordered.

Wrong command/top-level fields or shape yields {"issue":"bad-command"}. Invalid nodes, edges or graph shapes yield {"issue":"bad-graph"}. Validate the complete manifest before ordering. Emit one JSON result, exiting zero for these application errors.

Public smoke:
Input: {"command":"order","nodes":[{"name":"page","requires":["theme"]},{"name":"theme","requires":[]},{"name":"icon","requires":[]}]}
Output: {"ordered":["theme","page","icon"],"blocked":[]}

Extend the asset-manifest checker in tool.py with target dependency closure and a deterministic ordering correction. Preserve the graph validation and JSON fault contracts. Standard library only; no real builds, installs, network or persistent state.

Ordering correction: replace the old manifest-position ready-node tie break in every operation. Whenever several nodes are ready, emit the lexicographically smallest name, reconsidering readiness after each single emission. This changes ordered, not the previously defined blocked diagnostic order.

Add {"command":"closure","nodes":[NODE,...],"targets":[NAME,...]}. targets has 0..32 distinct declared node names. Invalid target values, duplicates or unknown names yield {"issue":"bad-selection"}. Validate the entire manifest before restricting it to targets; an invalid disconnected node is still a bad-graph fault. Schema errors therefore take precedence over selection faults.

Compute the smallest set containing the targets and all their direct/transitive prerequisites. Return {"needed":[NAME,...],"ordered":[NAME,...],"blocked":[NAME,...]}. needed is lexicographically sorted. Order only the needed subgraph with the corrected tie break and existing blocked semantics. Unrelated valid cycles do not block the selected subgraph. Empty targets produce three empty lists.

The order command remains supported under the corrected tie break. Extra fields and unsupported commands remain bad-command. Current source and this correction override the former arrival-in-manifest policy.

Public smoke:
Input: {"command":"closure","nodes":[{"name":"site","requires":["style","script"]},{"name":"style","requires":[]},{"name":"script","requires":[]},{"name":"draft","requires":[]}],"targets":["site"]}
Output: {"needed":["script","site","style"],"ordered":["script","style","site"],"blocked":[]}

milestones.brief:
Add incremental rebuild impact to the asset-manifest checker in tool.py. Preserve order and closure, their current tie break and validation/fault contracts. Python standard library only; analyze the manifest, never execute a build.

New request: {"command":"impact","nodes":[NODE,...],"changed":[NAME,...]}. changed has the same validation as closure targets. Determine every affected node: each changed node plus every direct or transitive consumer of an affected node. Multiple paths must not duplicate nodes. Empty changed is valid. Validate the whole graph before selection.

Return {"affected":[NAME,...],"ordered":[NAME,...],"blocked":[NAME,...]}. affected is lexicographically sorted. Rebuild only the affected subgraph, following the current ordering and blocked rules. An unchanged prerequisite is assumed already available: do not add or schedule it merely because an affected node requires it. Valid disconnected cycles are irrelevant unless affected. A cycle among affected nodes may still block their affected consumers.

No new options or fields are accepted. Unknown/duplicate changed names are bad-selection; malformed graphs remain bad-graph; bad command shapes remain bad-command. Do not silently drop bad nodes while pruning.

Public smoke:
Input: {"command":"impact","nodes":[{"name":"page","requires":["style","font"]},{"name":"style","requires":[]},{"name":"font","requires":[]},{"name":"preview","requires":["page"]}],"changed":["style"]}
Output: {"affected":["page","preview","style"],"ordered":["style","page","preview"],"blocked":[]}
